MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL MEETING

  FEBRUARY 27, 2018

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order at
7:06 p.m. in the City Council Chamber, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, by MAYOR HUFF.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

MAYOR HUFF led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance.

ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman.

City Council Members Absent:  None.

City Staff Present: City Manager Doug Prichard
  Assistant City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Planning Director David Wahba
  Community Services Director Andy Clark
  Assistant to the City Manager Alexa Davis
  City Clerk Heidi Luce

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  RECOGNITION OF ROLLING HILLS ESTATES’ CLEAN BAY CERTIFIED RESTAURANTS

  Victoria Gambale of the Clean Bay Foundation provided an overview of the Bay
  Foundation’s Clean Bay Restaurant Certification program.

  On behalf of the Bay Foundation and the City of Rolling Hills Estates, MAYOR HUFF
  recognized fourteen Rolling Hills Estates’ restaurants as being Clean Bay Certified
  including Bristol Farms Café; Domino’s Pizza; Good Stuff; Giorgio’s Restaurant; The
  Habit; Jack Kramer Club; Luna Rossa Ristorante; MOD Pizza; Red Brick Pizza; The
  Original Red Onion; Rubio’s; Ruby’s Diner; TataWan Thai Cuisine and Yummy Yogurt.

  MAYOR HUFF and Ms. Gambale presented certificates of recognition to those
  restaurants with representative present including: The Original Red Onion and MOD
  Pizza.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
FEBRUARY 27, 2018
 B.  WEST BASIN MUNICIPAL WATER DISTRICT

  On behalf of West Basin Municipal Water District, Director Harold Williams recognized
  the City’s leadership and commitment to water reliability and provided an overview of
  the initiatives that West Basin is undertaking with regard to water reliability.

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR
  The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of
  the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by
  a member prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed for individual consideration will be voted on
  separately.)

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE ITEMS A-J AS PRESENTED BELOW.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

  Reading in full of all ordinances and resolutions presented for consideration to the City
  Council will be waived and all such ordinances and resolutions will be read by title only.

  APPROVED.

B.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF FEBRUARY 13, 2018

  APPROVED.

C.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS – FEBRUARY 2018

  APPROVED WARRANTS 59604 THROUGH 59643 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $144,581.61 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

D.  JANUARY 2018 SCHEDULE OF INVESTMENTS

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

E.  JANUARY 2018 REVENUE AND EXPENDITURE REPORT

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

F.  GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES OF FEBRUARY 6, 2018

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

G.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF FEBRUARY 20, 2018

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
FEBRUARY 27, 2018
 H.  AUTHORITY TO MICRO-IMAGE AND DESTROY ORIGINAL RECORDS – REQUESTS
  FOR ZONE CLEARANCE FOR MINOR WORK (APRIL-DECEMBER 2015)

  APPROVED AS PRESENTED.

I.  NOTICE OF COMPLETION FOR WORK PERFORMED BY CALIFORNIA PROFESSIONAL
  ENGINEERING SERVICES, INC. FOR THE RECTANGULAR RAPID FLASHING BEACON
  (RRFB) AND IN-ROADWAY WARNING LIGHT (IRWL) INSTALLATION PROJECT

  ACCEPTED PROJECT AS COMPLETE; AUTHORIZED FILING OF NOTICE OF
  COMPLETION; AND DIRECTED RELEASE OF RETENTION.

J.  ACCEPTANCE OF THE WORK PERFORMED BY ACCESS PACIFIC, INC. FOR STORM
  DRAIN IMPROVEMENTS ON JUNE’S TRAIL AT PALOS VERDES DRIVE EAST

  ACCEPTED PROJECT  AS  COMPLETE  AND  DIRECTED  RELEASE  OF
  RETENTION.

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

  Ritu Portugal, 8 Club View Lane addressed the City Council on behalf of the Rolling Hills
  Country Club Estates Home Owner’s Association to express concern with regard issues
  they are having with the Rolling Hills Country Club in that they have not honored the
  commitments made during the development process specifically with regard to the slope
  and landscaping/maintenance at the entry to the Country Club Estates neighborhood.
  She expressed further concern regarding excessive noise and parking issues during events
  at the Country Club.

  Michael Piro, 12 Club View Lane addressed the City Council to further explain the concern
  regarding the grading/slope area at the entryway to the Country Club Estates
  neighborhood.

  Following brief discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to appoint
  COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN and MAYOR HUFF to an ad hoc committee to work with
  the Country Club Estates HOA and the Rolling Hills Country Club to facilitate
  communication to address the issues raised.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS (7:30 P.M.)

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 02-18: ORDINANCE NO. 721 – AMENDING AND
  RESTATING CHAPTER 17.43 OF THE ROLLING HILLS ESTATES MUNICIPAL CODE
  RELATED TO CANNABIS FACILITIES, CULTIVATION AND DELIVERIES.

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) Open the Public Hearing; 2) Take public
  testimony; 3) Discuss the issues; 4) Introduce Ordinance No. 721 for first reading and;
  5) Close the Public Hearing and schedule second reading an adoption for the next
  regularly scheduled City Council meeting of March 27, 2018.

  Planning Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
FEBRUARY 27, 2018
   In response to COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN, Planning Director Wahba stated that
  the ordinance allows for only indoor cultivation of up to six plants.

  In response to MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL, City Attorney Davis commented that, as
  directed by the City Council, this ordinance is written to be as strict as possible given
  current State law.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR HUFF SO ORDERED.

  MAYOR HUFF called for public comment.

  There was no public testimony on this item.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL INTRODUCE ORDINANCE NO. 721 FOR FIRST
  READING, WAIVE FULL READING OF THE ORDINANCE AND SCHEDULE
  SECOND READING AND ADOPTION FOR THE NEXT REGULARLY SCHEDULED
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING OF MARCH 27, 2018

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

  City Manager Prichard read Ordinance No. 721 by title only.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES ACTION ITEM FROM MEETING OF FEBRUARY 20, 2018 –
  APPROVAL OF THE HILLS ARE ALIVE RACE CONSULTANT AGREEMENT

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve an agreement with Michael Hogue
  Productions to provide fundraising, promotional and consulting services for the 2018
  Hills Are Alive Race.

  Community Services Director Clark provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  In response to COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ, Community Services Director Clark
  clarified that the check for Mr. Hogue has been prepared, but it will not be released until
  the agreement is approved.

  In response to MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL, Community Services Director Clark stated
  that the agreement is the same as past agreements and has been approved as to form
  by the City Attorney.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
FEBRUARY 27, 2018
   In response to COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN, Community Services Director Clark
  stated that the agreement does not currently require the consultant to submit his
  expenses.

  Following discussion, it was the consensus of the CITY COUNCIL to direct staff to follow-
  up with the consultant regarding expenses.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL CONTINUE CONSIDERATION OF THIS MATTER TO
  THE NEXT REGULAR MEETING OF THE CITY COUNCIL.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR HUFF SO ORDERED.

B.  AWARD OF BID CITY HALL AND CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER RENOVATION PROJECT

  Recommendation: That the City Council award the Bid Schedule B “Base Bid” in the
  amount of $153,000 plus 15% contingency to Marjani Builders for City Hall Renovation;
  approve additional project costs for a total approved expenditure of $330,000; and defer
  action on the balance of the project.

  Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  Discussion ensued concerning signage (Additive Alternative Bid D.) Assistant to the City
  Manager Davis explained that this item includes mainly interior office signs.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN commented that the most important aspect of the
  project, to him, is the part that is accessible to the public – specifically the signage
  around City Hall and Council Chamber. Assistant to the City Manager explained that
  if the City Council wishes to proceed with the Council Chamber renovation (Additive
  Alternative Bid D), the construction cost would be $166,000 with a total cost $190,900
  of (including contingency.)

  COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN recommended that the Council Chamber renovation be
  included given that PEG and QUIMBY funds could be used which would have limited
  impact on the General Fund.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN commented that QUIMBY funds are currently in
  deficit. He noted that the Audit/Finance Committee is having detailed discussions
  regarding projected income and PERS obligations and took a more conservative
  approach to the renovation project.

  Discussion ensued concerning the various funds available, including QUIMBY funds.
  City Manager Prichard confirmed that the existing QUIMBY funds are committed to
  other projects.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL commented that the Audit/Finance Committee is
  reviewing competing capital projects and other obligations; and plans to discuss further
  with the results to be presented at the Policy Development Session.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
FEBRUARY 27, 2018
   Discussion ensued concerning the options before the City Council with regard to
  awarding the bid and the date and time of the Policy Development Session.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL AWARD BID SCHEDULE B “BASE BID” IN THE
  AMOUNT OF $153,000 PLUS 15% CONTINGENCY TO MARJANI BUILDERS FOR
  CITY HALL RENOVATION; APPROVE ADDITIONAL PROJECT COSTS FOR A
  TOTAL APPROVED EXPENDITURE OF $330,000; DIRECT STAFF TO ASK THE
  CONTRACTOR IF THEY WILL HOLD THE PRICE ON ADDITIVE ALTERNATIVE
  BID D FOR FUTURE AWARD; AND DEFER ACTION ON THE BALANCE OF THE
  PROJECT.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

9.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  PROPOSED AMENDED BUSINESS LICENSE TAX ORDINANCE AND CONSIDERATION
  OF RESOLUTION NO. 2415 ORDERING THE SUBMISSION TO THE QUALIFIED
  ELECTORS OF THE CITY A CERTAIN MEASURE ENTITLED “AN ORDINANCE OF THE
  CITY OF ROLLING HILLS ESTATES, CALIFORNIA AMENDING AND RESTATING
  CHAPTER 5.08 OF THE ROLLING HILLS ESTATES MUNICIPAL CODE PERTAINING TO
  BUSINESS LICENSE TAXES” AT THE GENERAL MUNICIPAL ELECTION TO BE HELD ON
  TUESDAY, JUNE 5, 2018 AND PROVIDING DIRECTION REGARDING PREPARATION OF
  AN IMPARTIAL ANALYSIS, ARGUMENTS AND REBUTTALS.

  Recommendation: That the City Council adopt Resolution No. 2415 taking the following
  actions: 1) submitting the ballot question contained in Section 1 to the voters at the
  General Municipal Election on June 5, 2018; 2) approving the text of the ordinance
  attached as Exhibit A; 3) directing the City Attorney to prepare an impartial analysis of
  the measure and; 4) establishing regulations an deadlines for submittal of ballot
  arguments; determining whether or not to allow rebuttal arguments; determining the
  authorized City officials who will prepare the ballot argument in favor of the measure
  and its signatories; and directing certain actions be taken to comply with Elections Code
  requirements for placing the measure before the voters.

  City Manager Prichard provided a staff report (as per agenda material). He noted that a
  letter was received from the Palos Verdes Peninsula Chamber of Commerce via e-mail
  today providing the Chamber’s position on several matters related to the proposed
  ordinance.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN suggested that the City Council review the letter point
  by point and discuss each item individually. The CITY COUNCIL concurred and
  proceeded to review each item.

  Phase In

  Discussion ensued concerning the suggestion that the tax be phased in over multiple
  years rather than all at once. It was noted that averaged over the number of businesses

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
FEBRUARY 27, 2018
   in the City, the increase per business is minimal. It was also noted that phasing in
  would not make sense for the businesses that are seeing a decrease in the tax.

  Following discussion, it was the consensus of the COUNCIL to leave effective date as
  currently proposed and to not include a phase in.

  CPI Adjustment

  Discussion ensued concerning the suggestion that the CPI rate be adjusted every five
  years rather than every three years as currently proposed.

  Following discussion, it was the consensus of the COUNCIL to change the CPI
  adjustment to every five years as well as the dates affected by that change.

  Residential Care Facilities

  Discussion ensued concerning the suggestion that rate for Residential Care Facilities be
  reduced to $2/$1000 gross revenue instead of $3/$1,000 of gross revenue as currently
  proposed. Further discussion ensued concerning the loss in sales tax revenue as a
  result of the entitlement given.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN suggested that the rate be put back to $4/$1,000 in
  gross receipts as originally proposed.

  Further discussion ensued concerning the loss of sales tax revenue and the proposed
  rate for Residential Care Facilities.

  Following discussion, it was the consensus of the COUNCIL to change the rate for
  Residential Care Facilities to $4/$1,000 in gross revenue.

  Retail/Restaurants

  Discussion ensued concerning the suggestion that the rate for retail/restaurants be
  reduced from .50/$1,000 in gross revenue to .25/$1,000 in gross revenue. City
  Manager Prichard commented that the rate currently proposed is the lowest rate of this
  type of tax and takes into account the sales tax generated by these business.

  Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to leave the rate for
  retail/restaurants as currently proposed at .50/$1,000 in gross revenue

  Increase certain tax rates if others discussed previously are decreased

  Following discussion concerning this suggestion, the City Council concurred to not
  make any further changes.

  City Manager Prichard noted that the ballot question will also need to be changed based
  on the direction. Discussion ensued concerning the Resolution.

  Following discussion, it was the consensus of the CITY COUNCIL to allow rebuttal
  arguments and to authorize Mayor Pro Tem Mitchell and Mayor Huff to make

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  7
FEBRUARY 27, 2018
   arrangement for the submittal of the argument in favor of the measure and determine
  the signatories.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2415 AS AMENDED
  TAKING THE FOLLOWING ACTIONS: ORDERING THE MEASURE TO BE
  SUBMITTED TO THE ELECTORS AT THE GENERAL MUNICIPAL ELECTION TO
  BE HELD IN THE CITY ON JUNE 5, 2018; APPROVING THE TEXT OF THE
  ORDINANCE AS AMENDED TO CHANGE THE CPI ADJUSTMENT AND THE
  RATE FOR RESIDENTIAL CARE FACILITIES; DIRECTING THE CITY ATTORNEY
  TO PREPARE AN IMPARTIAL ANALYSIS; ESTABLISHING DEADLINES FOR
  SUBMITTAL OF ARGUMENTS; AUTHORIZING THE MAYOR AND MAYOR PRO
  TEM TO SUBMIT AN ARGUMENT IN FAVOR OF THE MEASURE; PROVIDING
  FOR THE SUBMISSION OF REBUTTAL ARGUMENTS; AND DIRECTING
